title: Exactness and unique descent for module strict-local restriction
statement: For every commutative ring $A$, scheme $B$, geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and $g:S=B_{(s)}\to B$, in the small affine-neighbourhood model of [def-pur-module-strict-local-section-restriction], the module geometric stalk preserves finite limits, global sections on $S$ preserve finite colimits, and there exists exactly one natural transformation $r:s^*\to\Gamma(S,g^{-1}(-))$ whose composite with every representative affine pointed germ is the section restriction defined there.

source.place: Step 2: canonical module-valued strict-local comparison, constants, Kummer generators and restriction.

proof.text: First spell out the scalar passage, using the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If an abelian colimit has legs $c_i$ from $A$-modules, define multiplication by $a\in A$ as the unique endomorphism with $a c_i=c_i a$. The module laws follow by precomposing with all $c_i$, and the induced map to any module cocone is linear by the same test. Thus this abelian colimit, with these actions, is also the module colimit. Dually, an abelian limit has the coordinatewise action and is the module limit: its universal maps are linear after every projection. These arguments also show that a linear map whose underlying additive map is invertible is a module isomorphism. For sheaf limits the construction is sectionwise: compatible local sections glue coordinate by coordinate, so the resulting presheaf is a sheaf. Consequently forgetting scalars preserves and detects these limits. Applied to the neighbourhood colimit defining [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], the first construction identifies the underlying abelian module stalk, including its germ maps, with the abelian stalk. These are universal-property calculations, valid also for the empty diagram and the zero ring.

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] at the given geometric point of $B$. It preserves the finite limits of underlying abelian sheaves. By step 1 the underlying diagram of a finite module-sheaf limit is the corresponding abelian-sheaf limit, and the underlying module stalk is the abelian stalk. Hence the canonical module comparison from the stalk of this limit to the limit of the stalks is an additive isomorphism. It is linear because its composites with the limit projections are the stalks of linear maps. Its inverse is linear by step 1. This proves preservation of finite limits for the module stalk.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, representative-neighbourhood restriction construction; Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian

proof.text: Let $D$ be any finite diagram of $A$-module sheaves on the actual small-colimit scheme $S$. By [lem-pbc-u2-module-sheaf-underlying-preserves-colimit], its colimit cocone becomes an abelian-sheaf colimit after forgetting scalars. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-scheme-sections-exact] to this cocone: the abelian global sections on this very $S$ preserve its colimit. Module global sections have exactly these underlying additive sections, since they evaluate at the terminal object. By the module-colimit construction in step 1, the resulting module sections cocone is therefore a colimit too. In detail its universal additive map to a module cocone commutes with multiplication by every $a$ after each colimit leg and hence is linear. This proves the finite-colimit assertion, including the empty diagram, without any finiteness hypothesis on $B$.

proof.text:
Use the initial small representative diagram and compatible geometric sections supplied by [def-weil-pbc-small-strict-local-section-cone]. The representatives form the small full subcategory of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] of the cofiltered category of pointed neighbourhoods, and every pointed neighbourhood receives a pointed map from one of them. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1) shows that the stalk colimit of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is computed on precisely the representatives in the statement: their germs form a colimit cocone. Write $H=g^{-1}F$, let $\eta_F:F\to g_*H$ be the adjunction unit, and let $\sigma_i:S\to V_i\times_B S$ be the supplied sections. For a pointed transition $t:V_i\to V_j$, their compatibility says $(t\times_B S)\sigma_i=\sigma_j$. Before the final terminal-object comparison, the component $d_i$ of [def-pur-module-strict-local-section-restriction] is $H(\sigma_i)\eta_{F,V_i}$. Naturality of the unit and contravariant functoriality give the full cocone equation
$$d_i F(t)=H(\sigma_i)H(t\times_B S)\eta_{F,V_j}=H((t\times_B S)\sigma_i)\eta_{F,V_j}=d_j.$$
All maps are $A$-linear. The common terminal-object/global-sections isomorphism preserves this equation. By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], there is a unique linear $r_F:F_s\to\Gamma(S,g^{-1}F)$ with $r_F\iota_i=d_i$ for every representative germ $\iota_i$. Only the geometric compatibility assertion of the small-cone node is used here; its abelian descent assertion is not substituted for module descent.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, representative-neighbourhood restriction construction; Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian

proof.text: For a morphism of module sheaves $\alpha:F\to F\prime$, naturality of the adjunction unit, of restriction, and of the terminal-object comparison in [def-pur-module-strict-local-section-restriction] gives $\Gamma(S,g^{-1}\alpha)d_{i,F}=d_{i,F\prime}\alpha_{V_i}$. Consequently the two maps $\Gamma(S,g^{-1}\alpha)r_F$ and $r_{F\prime}\alpha_s$ agree after every representative germ. The colimit uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] makes them equal. Thus the $r_F$ form the required natural transformation. Any other natural transformation satisfying the germ equations has each component equal to $r_F$ by the same uniqueness; equality of components is equality of natural transformations. Together with steps 2 and 3 this proves all three assertions.
